memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "If you buy a Hebrew servant, he is to serve you for six years. But in the seventh year, he shall go free, without paying anything." - Exodus 21:2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
In the ancient world, slavery was everywhere, and it was usually permanent and brutal. Into that harsh reality God speaks a startling word: among His people, servitude must have a limit. A Hebrew servant could not be held forever. On the seventh year he walked out free, owing nothing. God was already planting seeds of dignity and release in a world that knew none.

This law was not God's endorsement of slavery but His way of restraining and softening a broken human system, bending it toward freedom. And notice the picture forming here — release in the seventh year, freedom without a price paid by the one set free. It quietly points ahead to a greater freedom. We were all once in bondage, not to a master with a whip but to sin itself. And Christ came to set us free, not after six years of labour, but by paying the price Himself (John 8:36).

If you feel trapped today — by habits, by shame, by fear — remember that God's heart has always leaned toward liberation. He is not a God who leaves people in chains.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
What still holds me in bondage that Christ longs to set me free from?
Do I extend freedom and grace to those under my authority?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that Your heart bends toward freedom. Break the chains that still bind me and help me lead others gently toward the liberty You give. Amen.
